sentences.text: The genus Wannia contains only one species, Wannia scurriensis, known from a single specimen. This holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skull housed at Texas Tech University.
Unlike other phytosaurs, Wannia has basitubera at the base of the skull that are widely separated. It also features a swelling on the nasal bone behind the posterior borders of the nares.

Wannia was first described by Dr. Wann Langston Jr. in 1949 as a species of Paleorhinus. The genus name Wannia was proposed by Michelle R. Stocker in 2013. The genus name honors Dr. Wann Langston Jr., and the species name refers to Scurry County where the holotype was discovered.
The holotype was collected near Lake Alan Henry in the Camp Springs Formation of the Dockum Group.

Wannia is classified as a reptile. It belongs to the parent group Parasuchidae and is classified within the family Parasuchidae. Wannia is classified as the most basal known phytosaur based on five unique traits revealed by its re-description.
The most probable age for the formation containing Wannia fossils is the latest Carnian or early Norian. Wannia lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
